title: Comparison of derived local restriction with exact inverse image and slice restriction
statement:
Let $g:S\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $U$ an object of $S_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Use the actual inverse-image ring $R'=g^{-1}R$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] and its restriction $R'_U$ to the slice over $U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Write $F_g:\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\operatorname{Mod}(R')$ for module inverse image without extension to a different coefficient ring, and $G_U:\operatorname{Mod}(R')\to\operatorname{Mod}(R'_U)$ for slice restriction. These are exact. For $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(R))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], choose the localization representative $C$ of $DF_g(K)$ and define $L_{g,U}(K)=Q_U(G_U C)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction]. There is a comparison
$$DG_U(DF_gK)\xrightarrow{\sim}L_{g,U}(K)$$
obtained from the localization representative isomorphism and the exact-functor localization factor [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], which also defines $DF_g$ and $DG_U$. It transports morphisms and isomorphisms of $K$ functorially and is compatible with the natural isomorphisms
$$G_UF_gH^q(K)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(L_{g,U}K),\qquad L_{g,U}(M[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}(G_UF_gM)[r].$$
Here $q,r\in\mathbf Z$, $M$ is any $R$-module sheaf, and $M[r]$ is its degree-zero complex shifted by $r$. No immersion, flatness, boundedness, or equality between $g^{-1}R$ and another scheme's completed coefficient ring is assumed.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor: exact functors on unbounded derived categories), applied to actual inverse-image and localized module restriction; Bhatt–Scholze Proposition 6.8.11(3), implicit local cohomology comparison. The representative normalization is the DAG ringed-site-derived-restriction convention.

proof.text: Write F for actual-ring module inverse image and V for the target module-to-abelian-sheaf functor. The comparison [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-module-inverse-image-comparison] identifies F followed by V with the source forgetful functor followed by abelian inverse image. For the base-change functor of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], finite-limit preservation gives representable flatness; the generic flat left-Kan-extension and sheafification instances give finite-limit preservation of abelian inverse image. Its adjunction gives finite-colimit preservation and, since direct image is additive sectionwise, additivity. The module forgetful functors are faithful, conservative and preserve finite limits and finite colimits [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful]. Transfer additivity and finite-limit/finite-colimit preservation along the comparison, then reflect them through V. This proves inverseImage_exact, with no hypothesis on g or change of coefficient ring.

source.place: Tags 03D2 and 03DA; the flat Kan-extension implementation is WeilConjectures.Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Functor.Flat and the site pullback instances.

proof.text: For G equal to the existing slice restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], apply the universe-independent ringedOverFunctor_exactGeneral interface [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. It gives additivity and preservation of finite limits and finite colimits for precisely the existing source ring and restricted ring, without identifying object and Hom universes.

source.place: Section 03DH and Tag 04IX: localization of a ringed site.

proof.text: Apply exact-functor localization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to F and G. For X=DF(K), let C and epsilon:Q(C) isomorphic to X be the chosen localization representative [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The existing comparison is DG(epsilon inverse), followed by the factorization at C; its target is exactly the recorded representative restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-derived-restriction]. Use Mathlib Functor.copyObj on DF followed by DG with these objectwise isomorphisms. Its map is alpha_K inverse followed by DG(DF(a)) followed by alpha_K-prime; the functor laws and natural isomorphism are supplied by copyObj and isoCopyObj. Object equality and the specified comparison equation follow by reflexivity and the identity isomorphism laws.

source.place: Tag 015F: every complex computes an exact derived functor; representative conjugation is implemented by Mathlib CategoryTheory.NatIso, Functor.copyObj and isoCopyObj.

proof.text: For each integer q, take the canonical derived homology isomorphism h_F and h_G, descended from the exact-functor complex-cohomology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology]. Whisker h_F on the right by G and h_G on the left by DF, then whisker alpha on the right by H^q. Their composite is the required natural isomorphism, with component G(h_F) followed by h_G followed by H^q(alpha). The displayed component equality is definitional.

source.place: Tag 010N; derived.tex Tag 015F. The canonical descent is mapDerivedCategoryHomologyFunctorIso in the adopted source library.

proof.text: For each integer r, first whisker alpha inverse by the degree-zero single functor followed by shift r. Compose with the DF shift isomorphism mapped through DG and then the DG shift isomorphism. Finally compose with the shift of the DG-image of the F single comparison followed by the G single comparison. These are natural isomorphisms, so their composite gives the required natural shifted-single isomorphism. Expand whiskering and composition, distribute the shift functor over the last composite, and reassociate to obtain exactly the stated component formula. The canonical commShiftIso already includes both positive and negative shifts and their signs.

source.place: Tag 015F, exact termwise derived functors; canonical commShiftIso and mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor.
